title: Farnè 2002 · auditory–tactile extinction
citation: Farnè, A., & Làdavas, E. (2002). Auditory Peripersonal Space in Humans. Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience, 14(7), 1030–1043.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

cohort.scope: Right-hemisphere stroke patients with left tactile extinction and preserved unilateral neck sensation.

published_method.apparatus: Ear-level loudspeaker can occupy the right-front or right-back quadrant at 45° from the sagittal plane. Compare 20 and 70 cm from the head.
published_method.stimulus: The examiner's touch sensor gates wideband white noise or a 1500 Hz tone. Contact is shorter than 1 second. The level was set to 70 dB at the ear.

trial_families: Paired left touch and right sound

published_method.response: Report left, right, both or none without identifying the modality. Compare left-touch detection accuracy across touch-only, near and far trials.

stimulus_type.source: MIT Press version of record pp. 1040–1041, Materials and Procedure

implementation_gaps: The original contact-gated waveform, wideband limits, trial order, touch force, and measured physical onset offsets are unavailable.
The published task requires a contact sensor controlling a calibrated physical loudspeaker, clinician-led manual stimulation of the lateral neck, and coding of four verbal response alternatives.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
